data.name: VibeUE.NiagaraEmitterService
data.description:
Niagara Emitter Service - Python API for emitter color + module authoring.

Methods this service actually exposes (issue #462 — the docstring previously listed
renderer/module-input/script-discovery actions that are not bound):

Color authoring:
- set_color_tint(system_path, emitter_name, color[, hue_shift]) — handles ColorFromCurve
- get_color_curve_keys(system_path, emitter_name)
- set_color_curve_keys(system_path, emitter_name, keys)
- shift_color_hue(system_path, emitter_name, degrees)

Modules / parameters:
- list_modules(system_path, emitter_name, stage)
- add_module(system_path, emitter_name, module_script_path, stage)
- get_rapid_iteration_parameters(system_path, emitter_name, stage)

For emitter add/copy/duplicate/remove/move and renderer CRUD, use the engine
NiagaraToolsets via call_tool (see UNiagaraService notes). Scratch-pad / Custom-HLSL
graph authoring is on NiagaraScratchPadService.

Python Usage:
  import unreal

  # List modules
  modules = unreal.NiagaraEmitterService.list_modules("/Game/VFX/NS_Fire", "Sparks", "Update")

  # Add a module
  unreal.NiagaraEmitterService.add_module("/Game/VFX/NS_Fire", "Sparks",
      "/Niagara/Modules/Update/Size/ScaleSpriteSize", "Update")

  # Set color tint (works even with ColorFromCurve)
  unreal.NiagaraEmitterService.set_color_tint("/Game/VFX/NS_Fire", "Flames", "(0.0, 3.0, 0.0)")

tools.description:
Shift the hue of a ColorFromCurve module while preserving luminosity and saturation.

This is the recommended method for artistic color changes (e.g., orange fire to green fire)
as it preserves all the detail and gradients in the original effect.
tools.name: VibeUE.NiagaraEmitterService.ShiftColorHue

systemPath.description: Full path to the Niagara system

emitterName.description: Name of the emitter containing the ColorFromCurve module

returnValue.description: True if successful Example: # Shift orange fire to green (preserves all gradients and detail) unreal.NiagaraEmitterService.shift_color_hue("/Game/VFX/NS_Fire", "Flames", 120) # Shift to blue unreal.NiagaraEmitterService.shift_color_hue("/Game/VFX/NS_Fire", "Flames", 240)

tools.description:
Set an emitter's simulation target (CPU vs GPU compute).

GPU-only data interfaces (Grid2DCollection, Grid3DCollection, RenderTarget2D, ...)
make a CPU emitter's system invalid at compile time — switch the emitter to
"GPU" before wiring them. The system is recompiled after the change; on compile
errors check NiagaraScratchPadService.get_compile_messages.
tools.name: VibeUE.NiagaraEmitterService.SetSimTarget

systemPath.description: Full path to the Niagara system

returnValue.description: True if the target was set (or already matched) and the recompile ran Example: unreal.NiagaraEmitterService.set_sim_target("/Game/VFX/NS_TrackPainter", "Painter", "GPU")

tools.description:
Set a color tint on an emitter, handling ColorFromCurve modules automatically.

This method adds a ScaleColor module (if needed) and sets its Scale RGB value.
Works even when ColorFromCurve is present - the tint multiplies with the curve output.
tools.name: VibeUE.NiagaraEmitterService.SetColorTint

systemPath.description: Full path to the Niagara system

rGB.description: Color as "(R, G, B)" string. Values >1 make colors brighter.

returnValue.description: True if successful Example: # Make fire green (works even with ColorFromCurve) unreal.NiagaraEmitterService.set_color_tint("/Game/VFX/NS_Fire", "Flames", "(0.0, 3.0, 0.0)") # Make smoke purple with 50% alpha unreal.NiagaraEmitterService.set_color_tint("/Game/VFX/NS_Fire", "Smoke", "(2.0, 0.0, 2.0)", 0.5)

tools.description:
Set the color curve keyframes on a ColorFromCurve module.

Replaces all existing keyframes with the provided array.
Each keyframe must have time and RGBA values.
tools.name: VibeUE.NiagaraEmitterService.SetColorCurveKeys

systemPath.description: Full path to the Niagara system

emitterName.description: Name of the emitter containing the ColorFromCurve module

time.description: Time position of this keyframe (typically 0.0 to 1.0 for particle lifetime)

r.description: Red channel value (can be >1.0 for HDR)

g.description: Green channel value (can be >1.0 for HDR)

b.description: Blue channel value (can be >1.0 for HDR)

keys.description: Array of color curve keyframes to set

returnValue.description: True if successful Example: # Read, modify, write back keys = unreal.NiagaraEmitterService.get_color_curve_keys("/Game/VFX/NS_Fire", "Flames") # ... modify keys ... unreal.NiagaraEmitterService.set_color_curve_keys("/Game/VFX/NS_Fire", "Flames", keys)

tools.description:
Get all rapid iteration parameters from an emitter's scripts.
Rapid iteration parameters are module input values that can be changed at runtime.
tools.name: VibeUE.NiagaraEmitterService.GetRapidIterationParameters

systemPath.description: Full path to the Niagara system

scriptType.description: Optional: Filter by script type (EmitterSpawn, EmitterUpdate, ParticleSpawn, ParticleUpdate, or empty for all)

returnValue.description: Array of parameter info structs with name, type, and value Example: params = unreal.NiagaraEmitterService.get_rapid_iteration_parameters("/Game/VFX/NS_Fire", "Sparks", "EmitterUpdate")

tools.description:
Get the color curve keyframes from a ColorFromCurve module.

Returns an array of keyframes, each containing time and RGBA values.
This allows reading the actual curve data for analysis or modification.
tools.name: VibeUE.NiagaraEmitterService.GetColorCurveKeys

systemPath.description: Full path to the Niagara system

emitterName.description: Name of the emitter containing the ColorFromCurve module

time.description: Time position of this keyframe (typically 0.0 to 1.0 for particle lifetime)

r.description: Red channel value (can be >1.0 for HDR)

g.description: Green channel value (can be >1.0 for HDR)

b.description: Blue channel value (can be >1.0 for HDR)

returnValue.description: Array of color curve keyframes Example: keys = unreal.NiagaraEmitterService.get_color_curve_keys("/Game/VFX/NS_Fire", "Flames") for key in keys: print(f"Time {key.time}: R={key.r}, G={key.g}, B={key.b}, A={key.a}")
